---
title: "Methods and sources"
---

mortensor implements published methods. This page lists, for every method
of the package, its source and how the implementation relates to it:

* **published**: the method as published (numerical safeguards aside);
* **published, deviations**: the published method with stated changes;
* **package-specific**: no published source is known to us; the help page
  says so. Package-specific methods are never the default unless stated
  here, and deprecated ones warn when used.

The help page of each function gives the details and the full references.
Corrections are welcome: a published source for a method listed as
package-specific, or a deviation that is not listed.

## Data and harmonisation

| Function, option | Method | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mt_as_exposure()` | person-years from population counts: the mid-year population, or the mean of the populations at the start and the end of the year (1 January or 31 December) | Preston, Heuveline and Guillot (2001) | published |
| `mt_data()` | deaths of unknown age distributed over the age groups of the same stratum and period in proportion to the known deaths | practice of the Human Mortality Database | published |
| `mt_fill_suppressed(hierarchy = )` | iterative proportional fitting of the missing cells to published totals, from the expected deaths at the pooled rate | Deming and Stephan (1940); Bishop, Fienberg and Holland (1975) | published, deviations: bounds of the suppressed counts enforced by clipping within each step (package-specific; no convergence guarantee once a bound binds) |
| `mt_fill_suppressed(lower = , upper = )` | cells that no published total covers: mean of the Poisson distribution with the expected deaths at the pooled rate, truncated to the bounds | none | package-specific |
| `mt_ungroup(method = "pclm")` (default) | penalised composite link model with the exposures as offset, 1D and 2D; the estimates are the fitted values (`preserve_totals = FALSE`) | Eilers (2007); Rizzi, Gampe and Eilers (2015); Rizzi et al. (2019); defaults of the ungroup package; in 2D, the products with the tensor basis in array form of Currie, Durban and Eilers (2006) | published, deviations: cubic B-spline basis (the paper uses one coefficient per age and allows B-splines); smoothing parameter by BIC, the default of the ungroup package (the paper: AIC, `criterion = "aic"`); an open group of counts ends at `omega` without the paper's group with 0 counts beyond the maximum age; iterations stop at a relative change of the coefficients below 1e-6 or of the penalised deviance below 1e-8, with step halving (the paper: coefficients below 1e-6); in 2D both smoothing parameters are chosen by BIC (ungroup fixes them) |
| `mt_ungroup(open_split = "pclm")` (default) | the exposure of an open age interval of the grid split over single years up to `omega` by the PCLM of the exposures of all grid cells, with a group of 0 counts of 15 years beyond `omega`, as the paper ungroups grouped exposures | Rizzi, Gampe and Eilers (2015) | published |
| `mt_ungroup(open_split = "stationary")` | the exposure of an open age interval of the grid split over single years up to `omega` with stationary-population weights of the fitted rates, iterated with the fit | none | package-specific, opt-in |
| `mt_ungroup(preserve_totals = TRUE)` | estimates rescaled to the observed group totals after the fit | none | package-specific, opt-in |
| `mt_ungroup(method = "monotone")`, `exposure_method = "monotone"` | monotone cubic interpolation of cumulative counts | Hyman (1983) | published |
| `mt_ungroup(method = "hyman_kannisto", "natural_gompertz", "gam")` | spline heuristics with parametric tails (Kannisto tails fitted by least squares to log rates) | none | package-specific, deprecated |
| `mt_disaggregate(method = "shape")` (default), `mt_shape_rates()` | forecast draws of age groups split by a fixed age shape within each group, from the rates of the last observed years | none | package-specific (default) |
| `mt_disaggregate(method = "hyman_kannisto", "natural_gompertz")`, `mt_shape_rates(method = "gam")` | splines through the group rates of each draw; age shapes from an extrapolated GAM surface | none | package-specific, deprecated |
| `mt_smooth(method = "pspline")` | Poisson P-splines over age, or age and time, smoothing parameters by BIC; an open age interval of the grid expanded into single years up to `omega`, its exposure split as `mt_ungroup(open_split = "pclm")` | Currie, Durban and Eilers (2004); Rizzi, Gampe and Eilers (2015) for the split; Currie, Durban and Eilers (2006) for the products with the tensor basis in 2D | published |
| `mt_smooth(method = "whittaker")` | weighted Whittaker smoother of the log rates with the deaths as weights, over age or time, smoothing parameter by GCV for every fit | Whittaker (1923); Eilers (2003) | published |
| `mt_smooth(method = "gam")` | quasi-Poisson GAM with the exposures as offset, `s(age)` or `te(age, year)`, REML | Wood (2017) | published |
| `mt_smooth()` conventions | the first year of life is left out by default; an open interval is placed at its lower bound plus half the width of the interval below it (Whittaker smoother over age, GAMs) | none | package-specific conventions |
| `mt_smooth_check()` | Pearson estimate of the dispersion of the raw around the smoothed deaths | McCullagh and Nelder (1989) | published |
| `step_shocks()` | shock years removed or interpolated log-linearly before fitting | none | package-specific (interpolated years enter as data) |

## Models

| Function, option | Method | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lee_carter()` | Poisson log-bilinear model (default), or SVD with `k` re-estimated to the total deaths (`adjust = "dt"`), the deaths by age (`"dxt"`) or life expectancy (`"e0"`) | Lee and Carter (1992); Brouhns, Denuit and Vermunt (2002); Booth, Maindonald and Smith (2002); Lee and Miller (2001) | published; age groups without deaths get a constant rate, and the ridge and SVD fallbacks for sparse counts are package-specific safeguards that warn; with `adjust = "dt"`, years where the root search (package-specific bracket) finds no index keep the SVD index, with a warning |
| `lee_carter(choose_period = TRUE)` | fitting period by the ratio of the mean deviances of a linear and of the Lee-Carter index | Booth, Maindonald and Smith (2002) | published |
| `lee_carter(jump_off = "observed")`, `li_lee(jump_off = "observed")` | forecasts start from the observed rates of the last year | Lee and Miller (2001) | published |
| `lee_carter(jump_off = "observed", jump_off_years = n)` | forecasts start from the mean observed log rates of the last `n` years, placed at their midpoint and moved to the last year by the drift ("average n years observed") | Stoeldraijer, van Duin, van Wissen and Janssen (2018) | published; the paper does not state how the index of the midpoint relates to the fitted index of the last year, and the reading used reproduces its Table 8a for French men within 0.03 years |
| `lee_carter(jump_off = "filtered")` | forecasts start from the Kalman filter estimate of the index in the last year under the state-space Lee-Carter model (eq. 6): the variances, the drift and the initial level by maximum likelihood given `a` and `b`; the filtered index in closed form, equal to a Kalman filter with a diffuse start | De Jong and Tickle (2006) | published, deviations: `a` and `b` from the package's fit (the paper: maximum likelihood with spline age effects); the forecast keeps the drift and innovations of `lee_carter()` |
| `lee_carter(jump_off = "constrained")` | maximum likelihood fit with the forecast origin correction: `a[x]` the observed log rate of the last year and `k[T] = 0` (Appendix 2) | Li, Hardy and Tan (2009) | published; 0.5 deaths in cells of the last year without deaths, and no ridge or SVD fallbacks (package-specific) |
| `lee_carter(rotate = TRUE)` | rotation of the age pattern of decline towards an ultimate pattern (flat below 65) as life expectancy at birth rises from 80 to 102 (weights of eq. 2, exponent 0.5); the index solved again so that life expectancy at birth is kept | Li, Lee and Gerland (2013); Sevcikova et al. (2016) | published, deviations: weights from the life expectancy of each stratum (the paper: both sexes combined, with the coherent forecasts of Li and Lee 2005); every draw rotated with its own path (the paper: the median path); rates change from the jump-off year, from the fitted rates of the last year with `jump_off = "fitted"` (package-specific); the open interval closed with `L = l / m` (the paper extends it to age 130 with a logistic model); `b` from age 65 scaled as in MortCast (not specified in the paper) |
| `lee_carter(family = "nb")` | negative binomial deaths with variance `mu + phi mu^2`, one dispersion `phi` for all ages and years (Section 2.2); maximum likelihood (eq. 5) by uni-dimensional Newton updates of `a`, `b` and `k` (eq. 6-8) alternated with the estimate of `phi`; `k` a random walk with drift (Section 3.5); predictive draws negative binomial with the estimated dispersion | Delwarde, Denuit and Partrat (2007) | published, deviations: updates start from the Poisson estimates; `phi` by Newton steps on its logarithm with step halving, and 0 where the derivative of the likelihood at 0 is not positive (the paper: Newton steps on `1 / phi`, eq. 9); constraints `sum(b) = 1`, `sum(k) = 0` (not stated in the paper, consistent with its figures); draws with the uncertainty of the drift (the paper: point forecasts); with `bootstrap = TRUE`, negative binomial resamples (package-specific). Reproduces the paper's dispersions, drifts and standard deviations of `k` (its column labelled sigma^2 holds the standard deviation) and AIC for France within 1% from the HMD series in `demography::fr.mort` |
| `lee_carter(family = "nb", dispersion = "age")` | negative binomial deaths with one dispersion per age group, maximum likelihood (eq. 13, Appendix 1); with `bootstrap = TRUE` the parametric bootstrap of Section 3, whose refits keep the dispersions (step 2a); predictive draws negative binomial with the dispersion of each age | Li, Hardy and Tan (2009) | published, deviations: Newton steps on the logarithm of each dispersion with step halving, and 0 where the derivative at 0 is not positive (the paper: Newton steps on the dispersion); `k` a random walk with drift (the paper does not name its time series model); age groups without deaths keep a constant rate and Poisson deaths (package-specific). The estimated dispersions are biased downwards (about 7% in simulations) |
| `lee_carter(bootstrap = TRUE)` | parameters re-estimated on Poisson resamples of the fitted deaths | Renshaw and Haberman (2008) | published |
| `bootstrapped(type = "grid")` (default) | Poisson resamples of the fitted deaths on the grid, any model refitted | Renshaw and Haberman (2008) | published; models without fitted rates resample the deaths on the grid |
| `bootstrapped(type = "data")` | Poisson resamples of the observed deaths | Brouhns, Denuit and Van Keilegom (2005) | published, deviations: refitting the preprocessing in each replicate is package-specific |
| `rwd()` | random walk with drift on the log rate of every age; innovations resampled as age vectors of observed changes (default) or normal | standard benchmark, no reference given | published |
| `rwd(observation_noise = TRUE)` | moment estimator of a local level model with drift | none (the published counterpart is the model fitted by maximum likelihood; Harvey 1989) | package-specific, deprecated: use `arima_series(order = c(0, 1, 1), drift = TRUE)` |
| `p_splines()` | two-dimensional Poisson P-spline surface of the log rates over age and year, smoothing parameters by BIC; forecast by extending the basis over years with weight 0 in the forecast years, so that the penalty extrapolates the coefficients; draws from the normal approximation of the coefficients (covariance of the penalised likelihood); missing cells get weight 0 | Currie, Durban and Eilers (2004); MortalitySmooth 2.3.4 (Camarda) | published, deviations: for age groups, knots about five years of age apart, counted in the single years that the cells span (package-specific); the smoothing parameters by a grid search with steps of 1 on the log10 scale and a continuous search (MortalitySmooth: two grid searches with steps of 2 and 0.5); with `overdispersion = TRUE`, the dispersion stays in the penalty of the forecast fit and scales the covariance (MortalitySmooth's `predict()` refits without it and scales the standard errors) |
| `p_splines(overdispersion = "age")` | a dispersion for each age that varies smoothly over age (Model 3): the dispersions divide the weights of the fit and the deviance of the criterion; bias-corrected mean Pearson statistics by age, smoothed by penalised quasi-likelihood with the negative inverse link, iterated with the fit and its smoothing parameters | Djeundje and Currie (2011) | published, deviations: the second-stage dispersion `tau` by a Pearson statistic (the paper does not say how); the penalty order of the dispersion follows `pord`; only the bias-corrected scheme (the paper shows that the other underestimates the dispersion); predictive draws Poisson, as with `overdispersion = TRUE` (the paper gives no predictive distribution). Reproduces the paper's simulation of Section 5.1 (mean dispersion 2.395 against 2.4) |
| `p_splines(infant = TRUE)`, `cp_splines()` | coefficients of their own for the first year of life, penalised over years only | Camarda (2019) | published |
| `cp_splines()` | P-spline forecast held by asymmetric penalties within the central 95% range of the past rates of ageing and the central 50% range of the past rates of change of each age; residual bootstrap of the deviance residuals | Camarda (2019) | published, deviations: 100 bootstrap samples by default (`n_boot`; the paper: 1000); the basis over years of the fit extended over the forecast years, as the paper describes (the author's code builds a new basis over all years); cell ages, knots and the search of the smoothing parameters as in `p_splines()`, the rate of ageing at age 0 for age groups and the bootstrap deaths of cells without deaths are package-specific; predictive draws add Poisson deaths (the paper gives no prediction intervals of observed rates) |
| `arima_series()`, `ets_series()` | ARIMA or exponential smoothing model per age, chosen automatically or given by `order` | Hyndman and Khandakar (2008) | published |
| `arima_series(order = c(0, 1, 1), drift = TRUE)` | local level model with drift in its reduced form, maximum likelihood | Harvey (1989) | published |
| `hyndman_ullah()` | functional demographic model | Hyndman and Ullah (2007), via demography | published; smoothing without the monotonicity constraint where the monotonic spline cannot be fitted is a package-specific safeguard |
| `coherent_fdm()` | product-ratio method with functional data models: smoothed rates, geometric mean as product, weighted principal components (`beta = 0.05`), ARIMA scores of the product, stationary ARFIMA scores of the ratios | Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen (2013), via demography | published, deviations: the fractional differencing parameter of the ratios in [0, 0.5) (demography's default; the paper names -0.5 < d < 0.5); intervals by simulated paths (the paper: analytic variances for rates); ratios of each path rescaled to multiply to one and aggregates of a hierarchy outside the product (package-specific). `weighted = FALSE` is the unweighted default of `demography::coherentfdm()` |
| `product_ratio()` | product-ratio method with Lee-Carter components | none | package-specific, deprecated: use `coherent_fdm()` |
| `li_lee()` | augmented common factor model | Li and Lee (2005); Lee and Carter (1992) | published, deviations: AR(1) processes without intercept; their coefficient bounded at 0.99 (package-specific safeguard, warns) |
| `cae()` | common age effect model: log rates centred over the years, age effects common to the populations (orthonormal columns) by least-squares common principal components with equal weight per population, period effects of each population by projection on them; approximate BIC of eq. (5) | Kleinow (2015); Flury (1984) | published, deviations: the paper's criterion minimised by Jacobi rotations (Cardoso and Souloumiac 1996) from the eigenvectors of the summed matrices (the paper: the F-G algorithm of Flury and Constantine 1985 with the modification of Clarkson 1988); columns ordered by their variation summed over the populations (the paper: by one population). Package-specific: the forecast (the paper does not forecast): one multivariate random walk with drift of all period effects with correlated normal innovations and drift uncertainty, as StMoMo's for several indexes (Villegas, Kaishev and Millossovich 2018) plus the drift uncertainty of `lee_carter()`; 0.5 deaths in empty cells; `common_by` groups with their own age effects (an extension the paper names and leaves open); age effects from the bottom strata of a hierarchy |
| `cae(index = "coherent")` | forecast of the period effects by Model 3 of Table 10: the first period effects of all populations a random walk with one common drift, the others AR(1) processes reverting to 0 (a VAR(1) with diagonal matrix), so that the expected rates do not diverge | Enchev, Kleinow and Cairns (2017) | published, deviations: applied to the least-squares period effects of `cae()` (the paper: Poisson maximum likelihood with the constraints of its Table 4). Package-specific: the common drift as the mean change with equal weight per population (one per group of `common_by`), AR(1) coefficients by least squares through the origin bounded to 0.99, one joint covariance of the innovations, drift uncertainty, orders of 3 and more as order 2 |
| `saint()` | SAINT model, revised version: trend of pooled reference strata by a Gamma frailty model with Gompertz-type baseline and background mortality, fitted by pseudo-likelihood (EM estimates, profile likelihood of the frailty variance); excess slope and background random walks, level and slope a random walk with drift or (`ecm`) the restricted error-correction model of two groups; spreads of the targets on five piecewise linear age regressors, Poisson maximum likelihood per year, VAR(1) without mean (`spread_ar`: diagonal with coefficients in [0, 0.99] by default, unrestricted, or fixed); single ages from 20 | Jarner and Jallbjørn (2022); Jarner and Kryger (2011) | published, deviations: three misprints read as such ((B14), (B16), second line of (4.16)); common drift of the error-correction model divided by the number of changes; EM estimates computed by Newton-Raphson sweeps; package-specific: the search of the frailty variance, starting values, a lower bound of 1e-10 on the background rate, the estimators of the error-correction and diagonal VAR coefficients (bound 0.99, warns), independent innovations of the excess slope, the background and the targets' spreads, and regressors or `kappa` left out on age ranges narrower than 20-100; `background = FALSE` (trend without background mortality, a model of the class of Section 4.2) is package-specific and opt-in |
| `relative_model()` | subpopulations relative to a reference population: the reference by Lee-Carter or, with `cohort = TRUE`, the age-period-cohort model with the approximate constraint of Hunt and Villegas (2015); each subpopulation's log rates the reference's plus an age pattern of level differences and a common age pattern times its own index; all parameters by joint Poisson maximum likelihood; the reference index a random walk with drift, the subpopulation indexes a multivariate random walk with drift (`deviation = "mrwd"`), independent random walks (`"rwd"`) or constant (`"constant"`), the processes the paper compares | Villegas and Haberman (2014); Renshaw and Haberman (2006); Hunt and Villegas (2015) | published, deviations: the fitting steps of StMoMo's `rh(approxConst = TRUE)`, with an acceleration step for the age-period-cohort reference (package-specific numerics, same estimates; the Lee-Carter reference takes the plain steps); the reference as a stratum of the data or a separate `mt_data` object. The effective numbers of parameters match the paper's Table 1 for the models without cohort effects (171); with cohort effects the package counts 363 cohorts where the paper reports 353 |
| `coda()` | compositional Lee-Carter model of life-table deaths: index ARIMA(0,1,1) with drift, its first forecast step corrected to the drift; observed jump-off; draws by a bootstrap of the residuals and of the index paths; rates from age 80 by a Kannisto model extended to age 120; zeros replaced multiplicatively; coherent version with a common component from the mean death rates of the strata and ARIMA(1,1,0) deviations without drift | Oeppen (2008); Bergeron-Boucher et al. (2017) and their supplementary code | published, deviations: draws centred on the point forecast part by part, as in the authors' code (the paper shifts the bounds of life expectancy); `ceiling(sqrt(n_draws))` refits (the paper: 100 refits with 100 paths each); `a_x = n / 2` at age 0 (the authors' code: 0.06); the observed jump-off from the deaths of the last year without the P-spline smoothing that Appendix G mentions, as in the authors' code; zeros by the formula of Appendix C (the authors' code closes the composition after the imputation); without single ages from 80 to at least 89, the package-specific treatment of `open = "regression"`; an imputed share of at most 1/2 per year and a pooled Kannisto fit for years without one are package safeguards |
| `coda(order = , order_dev = )` | other ARIMA models of the indexes, for example the random walk with drift (`order = c(0, 1, 0)`) and AR(1) deviations with a mean (`order_dev = c(1, 0, 0)`) | Lee and Carter (1992); Li and Lee (2005) | published |
| `coda(open = "regression")` | the log rate of an open age interval regressed on the indexes; a closed age range ends with the survivors as a part (also the default where the age groups are not single years from 80) | none | package-specific |
| `coda_multiway()` | multiway compositional model: Tucker3 decomposition of the clr of the life-table deaths of all strata, each centred by its geometric mean over the years, ranks `c(1, 1, 1)`, least squares; time index as a random walk with drift; draws from the index with resampled innovations, other parameters fixed | Bergeron-Boucher, Simonacci, Oeppen and Gallo (2018); Gallo (2015) | published, deviations: estimation by higher-order orthogonal iteration (the same least-squares criterion); where the paper is silent: forecasts from the fitted deaths (`jump_off = "observed"` as `coda()`), independent ARIMA models for several time indexes, old ages, open age interval and zero deaths as `coda()`; single calendar years (the paper: five-year periods and age groups); the choice of the ranks by DifFit and the bootstrap of the parameters are not implemented; experimental |
| `coda_causes()` | multiple-decrement CoDa model for causes of death: the deaths by age and cause of each year as one composition, cause rates by eq. (7) | Oeppen (2008) | published, deviations: one component and the index model of `coda()` by default (Oeppen: two components and ARIMA(0,2,2) for Japan, `rank = 2, order = c(0, 2, 2)`); jump-off and draws of `coda()` (Oeppen gives point forecasts only); zeros replaced multiplicatively (Oeppen: light smoothing with an unstated parameter); the open interval as `coda(open = "regression")`, a residual cause for deaths the listed causes leave unexplained, and predictive draws that split Poisson all-cause deaths multinomially between the causes (package-specific); experimental |
| `coda_causes(weights = "deaths", rho = , individual = TRUE)` | 2S-CoDA: ages and causes weighted by their mean life-table deaths (eq. 10), years by `rho (1 - rho)^(T - t)` (eq. 11), joint components by a generalised SVD, and one individual component per cause from a plain SVD of its residuals (eq. 12) | Kjærgaard, Ergemen, Kallestrup-Lamb, Oeppen and Lindahl-Jacobsen (2019) | published, deviations: weights for all years `1, ..., T` (eq. 11 states `T - 1`, the text gives the last year weight `rho`); fixed ARIMA orders for every index (the paper: ADF test and AIC, settings not given); multiplicative zero replacement (the paper: half a death); draws by bootstrap refits with residuals drawn by part and years drawn in proportion to their weights (package-specific; the paper gives point forecasts); VECM-CoDA not implemented |
| `tucker3()` | three-way Lee-Carter model: Tucker3 decomposition of the log rates centred over the years, ranks `c(2, 2, 2)`, least squares | Russolillo, Giordano and Haberman (2011); De Lathauwer, De Moor and Vandewalle (2000) | published, deviations: estimation by HOOI (the same least-squares criterion); centring over the years only, as eq. (7) (the paper's Matlab session also centres across ages); the forecast of the period factors (multivariate random walk with drift; the paper leaves the model open; Bergeron-Boucher, Simonacci, Oeppen and Gallo (2018) forecast ranks `c(1, 1, 1)` with a random walk with drift of the index), `ranks = "bic"` or `"aic"` and 0.5 deaths in empty cells are package-specific; experimental |
| `tucker3(residual_noise = TRUE)`, `tucker3(transform = "coda")` | in-sample residual variation added to the draws; Tucker3 decomposition of transformed life-table deaths | none | package-specific: `residual_noise` opt-in (counts the observation noise twice), `"coda"` deprecated (its forecast of the period factors, open age interval and empty cells are package-specific): use `coda_multiway()`, the published multiway compositional model |
| `cause_shares()` | Tucker model of log-ratio coordinates of cause shares | none | package-specific, deprecated: use `reconciled()` or `coda_causes()` |
| `stmomo()` | GAPC models LC, CBD, APC, RH, M6, M7, M8 | Villegas, Kaishev and Millossovich (2018); Cairns et al. (2009) | published (StMoMo); `"rh"` is StMoMo's version with a cohort effect without age modulation; initial exposures of the logit-link models approximated as central exposures plus half the deaths, as `StMoMo::central2initial()`, and forecast probabilities converted to rates with `m = -log(1 - q)`; cohorts observed in fewer than `clip` cells get zero weight (`StMoMo::genWeightMat()`), and their fitted rates take the effect of the nearest estimated cohort (package-specific) |
| `stmomo("plat")` | reduced Plat model (period indexes for level and slope, cohort effect without level, linear and quadratic trend) with the logit link, period indexes forecast as a multivariate random walk with drift and the cohort index as ARIMA(2,0,0) with a constant | Plat (2009); Villegas, Kaishev and Millossovich (2018), the vignette's code | published; the vignette's logit link with initial exposures replaces Plat's log link with Poisson deaths, and the full model with a third period term for all ages is not offered |
| `apci()` | APCI model `log m = alpha(x) + beta(x) (y - ybar) + kappa(y) + gamma(y - x)` (eq. 8), Poisson maximum likelihood (Section 3) subject to the five constraints of Appendix C (over-constrained, Section 6), `gamma = 0` for cohorts with four or fewer cells (Appendix B); `alpha` and `beta` P-splines with second-order penalties and smoothing parameters by BIC (APCI(S), Table 1, Appendix D); `kappa` and `gamma` ARIMA models without a mean, orders by AICc and, for `kappa`, the order of differencing by RMSE (Appendix E); draws from the innovations of both processes | Richards, Currie, Kleinow and Ritchie (2019); Eilers and Marx (1996) | published, deviations: cubic B-splines with knots about five years apart and the search range of the smoothing parameters (as `p_splines()`), the constraints as Lagrange conditions of penalised IRLS (the paper: Currie 2013), the AICc of `forecast::Arima()`, the RMSE from the third residual and simulation from the state-space form are package-specific; the value-at-risk framework is not implemented. The unsmoothed model has the paper's 241 free parameters for 55 ages and 45 years (Table 2) |
| `bohk_rau()` | rates of mortality improvement of smoothed rates by age, with an exponential (default) or linear trend over time in a hierarchical Bayesian model; forecast improvements limited to 0.5-3.5% a year; draws from the quantiles of the forecast improvements | Bohk-Ewald and Rau (2017); Currie, Durban and Eilers (2004) for the smoothing | published, deviations: an MCMC sampler of this package (the paper uses JAGS); forecast improvements outside the limits set to the limits (the paper: implausible forecasts excluded "by setting thresholds"); the origin of the time index, the floor of negative improvements in the least-squares values of the exponential model, the knots of the P-spline surface, age 0 smoothed over time only, and forecast improvements kept below 1 are package-specific; convergence to reference populations is not implemented |
| `bohk_rau(draws = "samples")` | each draw is one posterior predictive path of the improvements | none | package-specific, opt-in |
| `nordpred_apc()` | age-period-cohort model of 5-year age groups and periods with a power-5 (default) or log link; drift projected with cut trend; prediction base chosen by goodness of fit; recent or average trend chosen by a test | Møller et al. (2003); documentation of the R package nordpred 1.1 | published (point projections agree with nordpred); annual data summed to 5-year periods and annual rates interpolated between the period midpoints, draws from the asymptotic normal distribution of the coefficients, the last cut of the trend beyond five future periods (nordpred: at most five), and the prediction base chosen with the log link when `link = "log"` (nordpred: the power link) are package-specific |
| `stanmomo()` | Bayesian GAPC models with a Poisson or negative binomial likelihood | Barigou et al. (2023), via StanMoMo; Delwarde, Denuit and Partrat (2007) | published |
| `apc_bayes()` | Bayesian APC model with random-walk priors, fitted where the deaths were observed | Schmid and Held (2007), via bamp; Knorr-Held and Rainer (2001) | published; the mapping of draws of age groups to the grid by shape factors is package-specific |
| `apc_select()` | choice of the random-walk orders by DIC | Spiegelhalter et al. (2002) | published |
| zero deaths | 0.5 deaths in cells without deaths in models of log rates | none | package-specific convention |
| `mt_order_strata()` | keeps an ordering between strata path by path | none | package-specific |
| predictive draws (`mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)`, backtests) | Poisson deaths given the model's rates; posterior negative binomial for `stanmomo(family = "nb")`; negative binomial with the estimated dispersion for `lee_carter(family = "nb")` | Brouhns, Denuit and Vermunt (2002); Delwarde, Denuit and Partrat (2007) | published |

## Combining models and coherence

| Function, option | Method | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ensemble()` | mixture (linear pool) of predictive distributions, equal weights by default | Gneiting and Ranjan (2013) | published |
| `ensemble(weights = "crps_stack")` | stacking of predictive distributions: simplex weights that minimise the mean CRPS of the mixture over held-out forecasts, an exact quadratic program in the kernel form of the CRPS | Yao et al. (2018, Section 2.1, eq. 2.2); Gneiting and Raftery (2007, eq. 21) | published, deviations: the CRPS as the scoring rule (Yao et al. allow any proper scoring rule and use the logarithmic score); the held-out forecasts are those of the inner rolling-origin backtest on the training years (leave-future-out, as in Barigou et al. 2023), scored on the log rates, in place of leave-one-out predictions |
| `ensemble(weights = "bias")` | weights exp(-\|bias\|) of the life expectancy projected for the last 13 training years; draws pooled in proportion to the weights | Kontis et al. (2017, Methods, steps 1 to 3) | published, deviations: life expectancy at the first age of the data (the paper: at birth); the projected value from the mean of the predictive draws of the rates in the observed age groups (the paper's code: the posterior mean rates); package-specific (reference unknown): one weight vector for several strata from the mean absolute bias over strata (the paper weights each population; use `stratified()`), the mean over several inner origins, draws assigned to components at random with the weights as probabilities |
| `ensemble(weights = "crps")` | weights inverse to the mean CRPS of an inner backtest | Shang (2012, Section 3.2.1): weights inverse to the mean absolute errors of point forecasts, following Bates and Granger (1969) | package-specific: the extension to predictive distributions (the CRPS of a point forecast is its absolute error), the log rates as the scored quantity and the use as mixture weights |
| `ensemble(weights = "stack")` (deprecated) | stacking of point forecasts, used as mixture weights | Breiman (1996); Kessy et al. (2022) | published, deviations: the weights optimise the medians and are used for the mixture; deprecated in favour of `"crps_stack"` |
| `ensemble(top_k = )` | trimming to the components with the lowest inner CRPS | none | package-specific; with `"crps"`, `top_k = 2` corresponds to the two best models of Shang (2012) |
| `stratified()` | different models for groups of strata | none | package-specific plumbing |
| `reconciled()`, `mt_reconcile()`: bottom-up, OLS, structural, WLS, MinT | projection of the draws onto coherent forecasts | Hyndman et al. (2011); Athanasopoulos et al. (2017); Hyndman, Lee and Wang (2016); Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos and Hyndman (2019); Schäfer and Strimmer (2005) | published, deviations: WLS and MinT weights from the variances and covariances of the base draws (the papers use in-sample residuals) |
| `reconciled(covariance = "errors")` with `"wls"` or `"mint"` | weights from the errors of inner forecasts in the training data: mean squared errors (WLS), or their sample covariance (errors of mean zero) with the correlations shrunk towards the identity (MinT) | Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos and Hyndman (2019); Wickramasuriya, Turlach and Hyndman (2020); Schäfer and Strimmer (2005); Panagiotelis et al. (2023) | published, deviations: one set of weights per age and horizon from the `h`-step errors of forecasts at `n_origins` inner origins (the papers: in-sample one-step residuals, proportional for all horizons); package-specific: forecast years beyond `horizon` take the weights of the last inner horizon, ages without errors those of the draws; opt-in (default `covariance = "draws"`) |
| non-negativity | for draws with negative bottom values, the quadratic program of the reconciliation with non-negative bottom values, solved by block principal pivoting | Wickramasuriya, Turlach and Hyndman (2020) | published; infeasibilities below 1e-10 of the largest base forecast of the draw count as zero (the paper: 1e-12) |
| `fixed = ` | nodes kept unchanged (immutable forecasts) | Zhang et al. (2023) | published, approximated by a near-zero variance (1e-10 of the largest); with `"mint"` the other nodes get their covariance conditional on the fixed nodes, so that the fixed nodes are equality constraints of the weighted least-squares problem, also in the non-negative quadratic program |
| `method = "proportional"` | top-down by forecast proportions | Gross and Sohl (1990); Athanasopoulos, Ahmed and Hyndman (2009) | published, deviations: one level, the proportions of the bottom forecasts below each fixed node |
| `method = "energy_score"` | score-optimal reconciliation: free `d` and `G`, total energy score, Adam with the paper's settings from OLS reconciliation | Panagiotelis et al. (2023); ProbReco | published, deviations: one `d` and `G` per age; inner models on expanding windows at `n_origins` origins (the paper: rolling windows of the final length at consecutive origins); horizons 1 to `horizon` in one objective (the paper: one horizon); observation noise in the training forecasts; 50 draws per step from a fixed set of inner draws, without replacement (the paper: 250, simulated afresh); ProbReco's stopping rule on the steps (the paper: on the gradients); rescaling before the optimisation and negative bottom values set to zero in the forecast (package-specific) |
| `coupled()`, `mt_couple()`, `reconciled(dependence = "ecc")` | ensemble copula coupling: the draws of each cell (age, year, stratum) of a base model reordered so that their ranks follow the draws of a template model; tied template values ranked at random | Schefzik, Thorarinsdottir and Gneiting (2013) | published (ECC-R; the paper recommends ECC-Q, which needs the quantile function of each margin), opt-in; coupling the draws of the models before observation noise, which predictive draws add independently per cell, is package-specific |
| `reconciled(dependence = "schaake")`, `mt_reconcile(dependence = "schaake")` | Schaake shuffle: the draws of each cell (age, forecast year, stratum) reordered so that their ranks follow the observed changes of log rates from distinct training years, the same years for all cells and consecutive years for the horizons; tied values ranked at random | Clark et al. (2004); Schefzik, Thorarinsdottir and Gneiting (2013, Section 3.4) | published, deviations (package-specific): the template holds changes of log rates from the start year of each date (the paper: observed values); deaths of 0 count as 0.5; with more draws than dates, blocks of draws of the number of dates, each shuffled with all dates (the paper: as many dates as members); opt-in (default `"none"`) |
| `reconciled(dependence = "empirical")`, `mt_reconcile(dependence = "empirical")` | Schaake shuffle with the stratum as margin: the whole path of each stratum in a draw (all ages and forecast years) is one member and moves intact; the members of each stratum are ranked by the mean annual change of their log age-standardised rate over the forecast years and take the ranks of the observed annual changes of the same summary in distinct training years, the same years for all strata; every stratum keeps its set of paths; tied template values ranked at random | Clark et al. (2004); Schefzik, Thorarinsdottir and Gneiting (2013, Section 3.4); reordering of bottom-level samples to an empirical copula: Ben Taieb, Taylor and Hyndman (2021), as discussed by Panagiotelis et al. (2023) | published method, package-specific (reference unknown): the stratum as margin; the summary (log age-standardised rate, standard population the mean exposure by age over strata and training years); the draws ranked by their mean annual change from the last training year; deaths of 0 count as 0.5; with more draws than dates, blocks as for `"schaake"`; fewer than three training years leave the draws unchanged, with a warning; opt-in (default `"none"`) |
| `recalibrated()` | spread of the draws rescaled by one factor for all horizons that minimises the CRPS of inner rolling-origin forecasts | member-by-member post-processing (Van Schaeybroeck and Vannitsem 2015); minimum-CRPS estimation (Gneiting et al. 2005) | published, deviations: the draws are rescaled around their median on the log scale, path by path |
| `recalibrated(scale = "horizon" (deprecated, use "per_horizon"), bias = TRUE, ages = , quantity = )` | power law of the factor over the horizon, drift correction, age bands, life expectancy and ASR as targets | none; analogues of another form: the bias correction in the predictive mean of EMOS (Gneiting et al. 2005, eq. 10) for `bias`, post-processing for each location separately (Van Schaeybroeck and Vannitsem 2015) for `ages` | package-specific, opt-in |
| `recalibrated(scale = "per_horizon")` | one spread factor for each horizon, each minimising the CRPS (or interval score) of the inner forecasts of that horizon; with `bias = TRUE` one shift per horizon | post-processing fitted to one lead time (Gneiting et al. 2005, sections 2c, 3 and 3a; Van Schaeybroeck and Vannitsem 2015) | published, deviations: the draws are rescaled around their median on the log scale; a horizon gets a factor only with inner forecasts of at least two origins, and forecasts beyond the longest such horizon stop with an error (package-specific requirement); opt-in |
| `recalibrated(method = "errors")` | median of the base draws plus h-step error vectors (all ages and strata of one inner origin) of the inner rolling-origin forecasts, resampled with replacement for each horizon and scaled by the tuning factor with which the central `level` interval covers that share of the inner errors | extrapolation of past forecast errors (Keilman, Pham and Hetland 2002); bootstrap intervals from h-step errors with a tuning factor (Shang and Hyndman 2017, section 4.4 of the preprint, pointwise version); joint bootstrap (Panagiotelis et al. 2023) | published, deviations: the model is refitted at each inner origin (Shang and Hyndman: principal components from all years); `n_origins` origins in the last `years` years (they use every year); the bounds come from the bootstrap distribution itself (the limit of many resamples); the errors are not centred (Keilman et al. assume a zero expected error); package-specific (reference unknown): the median of the draws as point forecast, origins drawn independently for each horizon (no block bootstrap), errors of observed log rates with half a death in empty cells, at least two origins per horizon; no coverage guarantee; opt-in |
| `recalibrated(target = "interval")` | interval score of one central interval | Gneiting and Raftery (2007) | published |
| `anchored()` | forecasts start from the observed rates of the last training year, with the offset kept in every forecast year | Lee and Miller (2001) | published (default) |
| `anchored(years = , decay = , shrink = TRUE)` | offset of several years, linear fade, empirical Bayes shrinkage of the offsets | DerSimonian and Laird (1986) for the variance estimator of the shrinkage | package-specific, opt-in; `years` is a variant of the averaged jump-off of Stoeldraijer et al. (2018), which `lee_carter(jump_off_years = )` implements |
| `mt_jump_off()` | step between the last observed or fitted year and the first forecast year | none | package-specific diagnostic |
| `tuned()`, `mt_tune()` | choice of settings by rolling-origin or hold-out accuracy; one-standard-error rule | Tashman (2000); Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (2009) | published, deviations: the standard error of the one-SE rule is approximate; `strategy = "two_stage"` and the minimum number of training years are package heuristics |

## Evaluation

| Function, option | Method | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mt_backtest()` | rolling-origin evaluation at the resolution of the observed deaths | Tashman (2000) | published; a cell without deaths counts as half a death (package convention) |
| CRPS from draws | empirical-CDF estimator | Gneiting and Raftery (2007); Grimit et al. (2006) | published |
| WIS | weighted interval score with the 23 quantiles of the COVID-19 forecast hubs | Bracher et al. (2021) | published |
| PIT | randomised where draws equal the observation | Czado, Gneiting and Held (2009) | published |
| MASE (`mt_score()`) | absolute error scaled by the mean absolute year-to-year change of the training data | Hyndman and Koehler (2006) | published |
| `mt_score(measures = "sape")` | standardised absolute predictive error `sqrt(pi / 2) abs(y - median) / sd` with the standard deviation of the draws; mean 1 for a correct normal predictive distribution | Raftery et al. (2013) | published; for life expectancy only, as in the source |
| `mt_score(measures = c("cov90", "halfwidth"))` | coverage of the central 90% intervals and mean half-widths of the 80%, 90% and 95% intervals (by horizon with `by`) | Raftery et al. (2013) | published |
| `mt_score(measures = "revision")` | mean absolute change of the forecast median of a cell between consecutive origins of a backtest | none; Stoeldraijer et al. (2013) name robustness to data updates as a purpose of a forecast without a measure | package-specific |
| `mt_dm_test()` | Diebold-Mariano test of one loss per origin: equal-weighted cosine variance with `0.4 T^(2/3)` cosine terms and fixed-smoothing t critical values (default) | Diebold and Mariano (1995); Lazarus et al. (2018) | published (the EWC test of a single restriction applied to the mean loss difference) |
| `mt_dm_test(varestimator = "daniell")` | fixed-smoothing test with the Daniell-kernel periodogram estimate, `floor(T^(1/3))` frequencies, t with twice as many degrees of freedom | Coroneo and Iacone (2020) | published; simulated size at nominal 5%: 4.9% to 6.0% at `h` 1-2 and 7.6% to 15.3% at `h` 3-5 with 7 origins, 4.8% to 13.8% with 15 or 16 origins (oversized where test years overlap) |
| `mt_dm_test(varestimator = "acf", "bartlett")` | the test of `forecast::dm.test()` with the correction of Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold (sum of the autocovariances, or Bartlett weights) | Diebold and Mariano (1995); Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold (1997) | published; no test (in place of lag 0) when the variance estimate is not positive |

## Results and derived quantities

| Function, option | Method | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `life_table()` | `q` from `m` with `a_x`, open interval `L = l / m` | Preston, Heuveline and Guillot (2001) | published |
| `life_table()`, `a_x` | `n / 2` for every closed interval (default) or given by `ax`; the age-0 values of Andreev and Kingkade (2015) used by the Human Mortality Database are not implemented | Preston, Heuveline and Guillot (2001); Andreev and Kingkade (2015) | published |
| `life_table()` safeguards | constant-hazard `q = 1 - exp(-n m)` where the formula exceeds 1; the last positive rate for an open interval with a rate of 0 | none | package-specific safeguards |
| `life_table(open = "gompertz", "kannisto")` | closure of the open interval by a Gompertz or Kannisto hazard fitted by maximum likelihood with binomial deaths of those reaching each age | Thatcher, Kannisto and Vaupel (1998) | published (reproduces their fitted parameters); the last `k` single-year ages (10 by default; the source: 80-98); without `exposure`, the numbers at risk are those of the life table (package-specific choice for schedules without counts) |
| `life_table(open = "makeham", "weibull", "beard", "logquad", "logistic", "perks", "lynch_brown")` | closure by the further hazard laws that Feehan compares, fitted by the binomial maximum likelihood of the Kannisto closure, with the integrated hazards of Feehan's Appendix E | Feehan (2018); Thatcher, Kannisto and Vaupel (1998) | published (reproduces the Weibull, quadratic and logistic parameters of Thatcher et al.); Weibull with age counted from 0 as in Thatcher et al. (Feehan's fits count age 80 as 1); Levenberg-Marquardt steps from several deterministic starts (Feehan: BFGS from one heuristic and ten random starts); log-quadratic hazard integrated by 20-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature |
| `life_table(open = "aic")` | each schedule closed by the law with the lowest AIC; needs observed exposures | Feehan (2018) | published (Feehan compares the models by AIC); closing a life table with the selected law is package-specific |
| `mt_open_check()` | the laws fitted below a cut age and scored above it by the binomial log-likelihood and the chi-squared statistics of the predicted probabilities of dying; AIC of the fits | Thatcher, Kannisto and Vaupel (1998, chapter 6); Feehan (2018) | published (reproduces their chi-squared and log-likelihood values for the cohorts of 1871-1880); numbers at risk `E + D / 2` from person-years (the source: numbers reaching each age) |
| `life_expectancy()`, `prob_dying()` | period life table | Preston, Heuveline and Guillot (2001) | published |
| `asr()` | direct standardisation on the age groups of the standard population | Eurostat (2013) | published |
| `asr(age_groups = "grid")` | standard weights shared evenly among the grid cells of each standard age group | none | package-specific, opt-in |
| `standard_population()` | European Standard Populations 2013 and 1976, WHO World Standard Population | Eurostat (2013); Ahmad et al. (2001) | published |
| `yll()` | period expected years of life lost with the remaining life expectancy at the average age at death; standard expected years of life lost with `reference_ex` | Murray (1994) | published, deviations: life expectancy at `x + a_x` interpolated linearly between the bounds of the interval |
| `mt_observed()` | Poisson bootstrap of observed indicators | none | package-specific construction (parametric bootstrap) |
| `mt_contrast()` | differences and ratios between strata, path by path, with the share of positive differences | none | package-specific summary of the draws |
| `mt_inequality()` | SII and RII from a weighted linear regression on the relative rank | Mackenbach and Kunst (1997); Moreno-Betancur et al. (2015) | published (identity link) |
| `lifespan_variation()` | e-dagger, entropy, Gini coefficient, variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, interquartile range | Vaupel (1986); Keyfitz (1977); Leser (1955); Goldman and Lord (1986); Hanada (1983); Shkolnikov, Andreev and Begun (2003); LifeIneq | published, deviations: variance and standard deviation measured from the conditioning age `at` (LifeIneq: from the first age of abridged tables); interquartile range by linear interpolation of the survival curve |
| `mt_decompose(method = "arriaga")` | symmetric Arriaga decomposition; causes by their implied sensitivity | Arriaga (1984); Riffe, Tursun-zade and Trias Llimós (2024) | published |
| `mt_decompose(method = "horiuchi")` | line integral of continuous change | Horiuchi, Wilmoth and Pletcher (2008) | published |
| `mt_decompose(method = "stepwise")` | stepwise replacement from the youngest age, averaged over both directions | Andreev, Shkolnikov and Begun (2002) | published, deviations: all causes of an age are replaced together |
| `mt_decompose(method = "kitagawa")` | rate and composition effects of the crude death rate | Kitagawa (1955) | published |
| `mt_decompose(composition = "radix")` | subgroup life tables blended at the radix | Riffe, Tursun-zade and Trias Llimós (2024); Vaupel (2002) | published |
| `mt_decompose(composition = "pooled")` | composition of pooled rates by the line integral | Horiuchi, Wilmoth and Pletcher (2008) for the line integral | package-specific parametrisation |
| `mt_excess()` | observed minus predictive deaths of a baseline model | Msemburi et al. (2023) and others compare with the expected deaths of a baseline | published idea; estimand (prediction interval of the realised excess), P-score quantiles and `p_positive` as documented |
| `mt_pessimism()` | pessimism of forecasts by cause: life expectancy of the all-cause forecast and of the summed causes and their difference, the m-ratio (eq. 6) and the contribution of each cause (eq. 13), path by path; for observed data the approximation from the distributions of deaths by cause in two periods (eq. 12 and 14) | Wilmoth (1995) | published, deviations: with an odd number of years the middle year is left out of the default halves; 0.5 deaths for causes without deaths in the first period, with a warning; intervals of the approximation from Poisson draws (package-specific). Reproduces Table 1 of the paper; the decomposition by age and cause (eq. 15-19) is not implemented |
